blocks.text: Ethiopia’s economy is growing strongly. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) forecasts real growth of 9.2% for the 2025–26 fiscal year. But renewed fighting in the north, high reconstruction costs and climate-related crop problems are threatening the country’s economic recovery. London-based financial analyst Abdulmenan Mohammed warns of the consequences of further escalation. “If there is a major conflict […] the current economic growth will not be sustainable,” he told DW.
